what: Crossline turns one continuous rotation into two perpendicular straight-line motions. A rotating carrier takes an outer shaft around a 20 mm-radius circle. Three external spur gears make a marker arm counter-rotate. Two opposite physical markers, each 20 mm from the outer shaft, then sweep 80 mm from end to end. Both outputs are passive: there are no linear guides at the markers. One motor drives a carrier while an external 16:8:8 gear train turns the marker arm the opposite way. Two opposite markers trace perpendicular 80 mm straight strokes using only rotary joints.
try: Select this example and run it; Reset before running again after manual motion.

Follow one coloured marker through a complete carrier revolution. It reaches each end of its 80 mm line once, crossing the centre twice. Follow the other marker: its line is perpendicular, and it crosses the centre whenever the first reaches an end.

Reset to the saved pose and run the finite example. Motor A moves to +1008° at 84°/s, driving two carrier turns at a nominal 60°/s. It pauses, returns to its starting encoder angle and finishes in hold. Count two complete back-and-forth cycles on each line during the outward leg, then two during the return.

Compare the visible arm with its marker points. The arm turns continuously in the opposite direction to the carrier while the markers reverse along their lines. A point trajectory and its supporting body's orientation describe different motions.
why: With the sun held fixed, two external meshes give N_out*(omega_out-omega_carrier) = N_sun*(0-omega_carrier). Here N_sun/N_out = 16/8 = 2, so the outer arm turns at minus the carrier speed in the fixed frame. The output centre contributes one rotating radius R, and each marker contributes an equal radius rotating in the opposite direction. Their sum cancels one coordinate; their difference cancels the other. The result is a pair of perpendicular straight lines.
matters: The construction demonstrates how circular motion can produce an exact straight-line path through geometric cancellation. Its gears set the angular relationship, and its two equal physical radii set the line shape. It needs no slider at the traced point. The same mathematical motion is known from a circle rolling inside a circle twice its diameter, but this model realizes it with external spur gears and a supported rotating carrier.
question: The carrier-to-output distance is 20 mm. Would placing the positive marker only 16 mm from the outer shaft still produce a straight line?
answer: It would trace an ellipse. Along the source-defined principal axes its semi-axis lengths would be R+r = 36 mm and |R-r| = 4 mm, so the complete ellipse would measure 72 mm by 8 mm. With r=R=20 mm, the minor semi-axis becomes zero and the full straight stroke becomes 4R=80 mm. This is a mathematical prediction for a separately rebuilt and checked marker mount.
further: The two physical marker points stay 40 mm apart on one rigid arm even though each traces an 80 mm stroke. Their midpoint is the outer shaft centre, which travels around the 20 mm-radius carrier circle.

In a common shaft-axis convention, the 16/8/8 train gives outer angular speed −1 times carrier speed and idler speed +3 times carrier speed. Relative to the carrier, those speeds are −2 and +2. Always name the reference frame when describing a planetary train.

The small idler does not change the final 2:1 sun/output tooth-count relation, but its size determines the required shaft positions. Here the pitch-centre separations are 30 LDU and 20 LDU, giving the required total of 50 LDU. One LDU is 0.4 mm.

The saved carrier begins at +6.428571° and the positive marker radius at −6.428571°, because the input pinion and carrier teeth require a valid mesh phase. Their average is zero, so the two lines remain aligned with the source core X and Y axes. The orange marker starts close to its endpoint and the green marker slightly beyond the centre; neither position is silently reset for the path prediction.

The keyed assembly may begin at a phase that rotates both line directions. If the source carrier radius points at angle alpha and the positive marker radius at beta, the line directions are (alpha+beta)/2 and ninety degrees from it. The paths and phases used for validation come from those source placements, not from a fitted line through recorded motion.

Compare Ellipse Engine, which uses perpendicular sliding guides, and Straight Eight, which uses a closed pin-jointed linkage. Crossline constrains the two angular motions with spur gears while both marker points remain free of guides.

Historical counterparts: Cornell Reuleaux Model S16, Hypocycloid Straight-line Mechanism (https://digital.library.cornell.edu/catalog/ss%3A29272012), and Brown movement 329 (https://507movements.com/mm_329.html). They use a fixed internal ring. The external-gearing family is illustrated by KevinKarney's own-work Goodman Tusi Couple (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Goodman_Tusi_Couple.webm). This package copies no source media or CAD.

The frozen 147-part source passed all 60 predeclared native checks with 791 recorded poses; the finite program completed in 25.30 seconds. Forward carrier +720.284257° produced passive arm −720.284034°. Measured forward strokes were 79.989346 mm and 79.989372 mm; maximum full 3D source-path errors were 0.000241 mm and 0.000287 mm. Four deliberately corrupted copies of measurement channels were rejected. See ../validation/evidence/ordinary/crossline-acceptance.json.

Ordinary preparation retained five dynamic LEGO bodies, four physical hinges and all three external gear couplings, matching strict preparation. Both source-defined marker positions and body angles were observed independently; no output trajectory was prescribed. These precision numbers qualify the nominal native model. Browser operation and a physical LEGO build remain UNTESTED, including real backlash, friction, axle flexibility and flexible cable routing.
formula: R = 50 LDU = 20 mm; N_sun/N_out = 16/8 = 2; omega_out = −omega_carrier. In aligned source phase: P_plus = O + (2R cos(q), 0), P_minus = O + (0, 2R sin(q)). Each full stroke is 4R = 80 mm. In general source phase, gamma = (alpha+beta)/2 and delta = (alpha−beta)/2; rotate the coordinate axes by gamma and replace q with q+delta. A +720° carrier leg gives −720° of outer-arm rotation and two full reciprocations on each line. For this motor placement, Delta_q_carrier = (5/7)*Delta_a_encoder: A+1008° gives carrier+720°; the return target is A0°.
